newsitem.title: USA: Report finds major errors by FBI labs in big cases.
newsitem.headline: Report finds major errors by FBI labs in big cases.

text.p: The FBI's crime laboratories made serious errors in providing evidence in some major cases including the Oklahoma City and World Trade Centre bombings, the Justice Department reported on Tuesday.

The report issued by the department's inspector general after an 18-month investigation recommended the removal of the heads of some laboratories and overhauling their operations. However, it also it questioned "the judgment and common sense" of suspended agent Frederic Whitehurst, who first accused the labs of scientific fraud and of slanting evidence to favour prosecutors.
"Most of Whitehurst's allegations were not substantiated," Inspector General Michael Bromwich wrote. "Some important ones were."
In detailing mistakes and flawed testimony, the report is likely to help defence lawyers in major cases such as the bombing of the Oklahoma City federal office complex in 1995.

It said that FBI officials involved in the Oklahoma City case "merit special censure" for relying on "unscientific and speculative" evidence about the size and type of the bomb that destroyed the federal court house. It said the evidence was based on what a defendant purchased rather than scientific analysis of the crime scene.

The two-volume report released by the Justice Department documented similar failings in such other high profile cases as the World Trade Centre bombing and the bombing of an Avianca Airlines jet in 1989.
